title: Derivation of Center of Mass of a Solid Uniform Hemisphere
governing_principles: Geometric circular disc slicing parallel to flat equatorial base
Pythagorean relation for thin disc radius r^2 = R^2 - y^2
assumptions: Axis of symmetry along y-axis normal to flat circular base

derivation_steps.description: Due to rotational symmetry about the y-axis, the center of mass must lie along the symmetry axis.

derivation_steps.equation: dm = \rho \, dV = \rho (\pi r^2 \, dy) = \rho \pi (R^2 - y^2) \, dy
derivation_steps.description: Slice the hemisphere into thin circular horizontal discs of thickness dy at vertical elevation y with disc radius r.

derivation_steps.equation: \int y \, dm = \int_0^R y \left[ \rho \pi (R^2 - y^2) \right] dy = \rho \pi \int_0^R (R^2 y - y^3) dy
derivation_steps.description: Set up the numerator first moment of mass integral from y = 0 (base) to y = R (apex).
Evaluate the elementary polynomial definite integral.
Express total mass M in terms of density rho and total volume.
Divide the first moment by total mass to arrive at the final centroid coordinate y_cm = 3R/8.

limiting_cases: y_cm = 0.375 R < 0.5 R (the centroid is shifted closer to the broader base, as physically required).
dimensional_check: Dimension of 3/8 R is [L], matching distance units.
source_provenance: HCV1 Ch 9 p. 152 Example 9.3; UP Ch 8 p. 286
